rules.title: File could not be parsed
rules.description: The file is not valid Python 3 (often leftover Python 2 syntax such as `except X, e:` or `print x`). It cannot be analysed or rewritten automatically.

rules.title: dict.has_key() call
rules.description: `d.has_key(k)` was removed from dict in Python 3; use `k in d`.

rules.title: Bare except clause
rules.description: `except:` also catches SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt; use `except Exception:`.

rules.title: Explicit `object` base class
rules.description: `class Foo(object):` is redundant in Python 3; use `class Foo:`.

rules.title: Old-style super() call
rules.description: `super(Foo, self).method()` can be written `super().method()` in Python 3.

rules.title: Deprecated typing aliases
rules.description: `typing.List`, `Dict`, `Tuple`, `Set`, `Optional`, `Union` can be replaced by `list`, `dict`, `tuple`, `set`, `X | None`, `A | B` (Python 3.10+).

rules.title: Missing type hints
rules.description: Function parameters or return value have no type annotations. Correct hints need human understanding of the code, so this is never auto-fixed.

rules.title: Python 2 except syntax
rules.description: `except ValueError, e:` is a syntax error in Python 3; use `except ValueError as e:`.
